key_insight: IQP-based quantum generative models can use genuinely quantum resources efficiently, with magic consumption better tracked from output distributions than from state-space distances.
engineering_relevance: For near-term and fault-tolerant quantum systems, this suggests a practical path to resource-aware generative circuits where two-qubit gates drive most of the useful quantum advantage.
method: Reframe progress using the probability simplex instead of Hilbert-space fidelity or geodesic metrics.
Measure resource use via changes in Jensen–Shannon divergence to quantify magic consumption.
Evaluate trained random γ-sparse IQP circuits and compare against phase-randomised states with matching sampling distributions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that trained random γ-sparse IQP circuits show signatures of efficient magic use, with the dominant contribution coming from two-qubit gates and unusually low intermediate magic.
watch_item: The framework is tied to trained circuit instances and distribution-level metrics, so hardware noise or mismatch between target and sampled distributions could weaken the observed resource-efficiency claims.
paper_title: Generative AI Beyond Tokens: Quantum Resource Consumption of IQP Circuits
